answer: An admission auction blocks fake agents by making entry scarce. Each epoch the network auctions slots; winners pay their bid as a burnt fee, and losers wait for the next horizon of sales. One honest agent anchors one bid near the clearing price, about 200 POA, and earns it back through work. An attacker needing 1,000 fake identities must win 1,000 slots, and its own bulk bidding pushes the price up, so the bill starts at 200,000 POA and rises per slot. That rising price, sweeping in like a gale, makes scale the attacker's cost while honest agents pay once and keep rewards undiluted.
